lines.t: Where can I buy a bus pass?

options: At the student center, on the first floor.
It costs forty dollars a month.
The bus passes every ten minutes.
I bought one yesterday.
optionNotes: Says when the listener bought one, not where.

lines.t: What time is your dentist appointment?

options: At the clinic on Park Road.
Two thirty, right after lunch.
I see her every six months.
Yes, I made one.
optionNotes: A yes/no answer to a wh-question.

lines.t: Do you have a pen I could borrow?

options: I borrowed a book last week.
I have a pen pal in Japan.
Sure, here you go.
It's open until six.
optionNotes: Correct: agrees and gives the pen.

options: It's next weekend, isn't it?
I went with my cousin.
I'll be working this weekend.
Really relaxing, thanks. I mostly stayed in.
optionNotes: Correct: describes how the weekend was.
questions.explanation: 'How was' asks for a description of a past event: D.

lines.t: Is there a vending machine in this building?

options: Yes, there's one by the elevators.
I'm sending it right now.
This building is very old.
I bought a snack this morning.
optionNotes: Related to snacks but doesn't answer.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question. A answers it and adds where the machine is.

lines.t: Who are you going to the game with?

options: It starts at seven.
A few friends from my dorm.
We're taking the bus.
Our team won last time.
optionNotes: Talks about the team, not companions.

lines.t: Could you open the window, please?

options: The shop opens at nine.
I'll close the door at night.
Of course. It is a bit stuffy in here.
There's a nice view from the window.
optionNotes: Talks about closing a door, not the request.
questions.explanation: A polite request. C agrees and gives a reason.

lines.t: I could've sworn the meeting was in Room two ten.

options: I swore I'd never be late again.
It was supposed to be, but they moved it to 214.
There were ten people at the meeting.
I couldn't find room for it in my bag.
optionNotes: Gives a number, not an explanation.
questions.explanation: 'I could've sworn' means 'I was sure (but I seem to be wrong)'. B explains why the speaker's memory doesn't match reality.

lines.t: You've got to be kidding. The café's closed for renovations?

options: No, my kids are at home.
The new design looks great, doesn't it?
I've got a coffee for you.
I'm afraid so, until the end of the month.
optionNotes: Correct: confirms the bad news with a detail.
questions.explanation: The speaker is surprised and asks for confirmation. D confirms ('I'm afraid so') and says how long.

lines.t: Remind me never to sign up for an eight a.m. class again.

options: I'll set a reminder for eight.
Rough morning, huh? You look exhausted.
Classes start again in August.
Never mind, I'll sign it later.
optionNotes: Correct: sympathizes with the speaker's complaint.
questions.explanation: This is a complaint, not a real request for a reminder. B sympathizes.

lines.t: If I'd known about the free tutoring, I'd have gone weeks ago.

options: I'm going to tutor weeks from now.
I knew it would cost a lot.
Well, it's not too late. They're open till the end of term.
I didn't know you were free.
optionNotes: Correct: encourages the speaker to go now.
questions.explanation: The speaker regrets not knowing earlier. C reassures them that they can still go.

lines.t: There's no way I'm finishing this reading by tomorrow.

options: Why not just focus on the first two chapters? That's what we'll discuss.
There's a way through the park.
I'll be reading in the garden tomorrow.
Yes, it was finished yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'There's no way...' means 'it's impossible'. A offers a useful strategy.

lines.t: I'm having second thoughts about the study abroad program.

options: The second program is in Spain.
Yes, it's a two-semester program.
I thought it was the first one.
How come? You seemed so excited about it last month.
optionNotes: Describes the program but ignores the doubt.
Correct: asks why the speaker has doubts.
questions.explanation: 'Having second thoughts' means 'doubting a decision'. D shows surprise and asks for the reason.

lines.t: I'd rather not walk back across campus in this weather.

options: Whether or not you go, I'm staying.
Want me to call a taxi, or should we just wait it out?
I'd rather have tea, thanks.
The campus is beautiful in the spring.
optionNotes: Correct: offers solutions to the speaker's problem.
Talks about campus but ignores the weather problem.
questions.explanation: The speaker indirectly says they don't want to walk in bad weather. B offers two practical options.
